zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 油價回落，美債在 CPI 公布前上漲

以色列與伊朗暫停攻擊，帶動原油下跌，加上科技股在美國通膨公布前走弱，美債週二上漲。10 年期殖利率下跌 3 個基點至 4.53%，大部分降幅來自損益兩平通膨率下降。$580 億 3 年期標售需求也較 5 月改善，顯示非農後提高的殖利率，仍能吸引資金承接供給。

這波反彈並未明顯動搖升息預期。期貨市場仍反映 Fed 年底前升息 25 個基點，選擇權買家則防範未來數月一次或多次升息。避險基金在 SOFR 期貨的淨空單創紀錄，若 CPI 不如鷹派預期，可能引發回補；現券客戶的部位則已開始轉向中性。

股市下跌時，信用市場需求仍在。騰訊較大規模的雙幣別發行吸引訂單，MSD Investment Corp. 以低於初步指引的利差完成發債，Shutterfly 卻必須在 12% 殖利率下進一步強化債權保障。美國以外，印尼緊急升息雖支撐匯率，債券仍大幅下跌。油價回落提供共同利多，但融資條件、當地流動性與政策信心，仍使借款人的處境各不相同。

## 通膨補償下降，升息押注仍在

交火暫停緩解眼前供給疑慮，WTI 下跌 3.40% 至 $88.20，布蘭特下跌 2.97% 至 $91.45。10 年期損益兩平通膨率下降 2 個基點至 2.33%，實質殖利率僅下跌 1 個基點至 2.20%。名目利率的大部分降幅因此來自通膨補償收斂，實質借款成本仍高：10 年期實質殖利率較一週前高 13 個基點，較一個月前高 27 個基點。

各天期名目殖利率降幅相近。2 年期下跌 2 個基點至 4.13%，5 年期下跌 3 個基點至 4.26%，30 年期下跌 2 個基點至 5.01%。2s10s 縮窄 1 個基點至 40 個基點，2s30s 維持 88 個基點。長債殖利率仍高於 5%，2 年期也明顯高於 Fed 的 3.5%–3.75% 政策區間。

過去一週，2 年、5 年、10 年與 30 年期殖利率仍分別上升 8、9、7 與 4 個基點，過去一個月則上升 23、24、15 與 6 個基點。月度曲線變化中，2s10s 趨平 8 個基點，2s30s 趨平 17 個基點。週二 2s5s10s 蝶式利差下跌 1 個基點至 −14 個基點，2s10s30s 下跌 2 個基點至 −8 個基點。5 年期實質殖利率持平於 1.82%，7 年、20 年與 30 年期則下跌 1 至 2 個基點。

隔夜利率選擇權中，有些部位押注 9 月前升息一次，甚至兩次。避險基金在就業報告前已建立創紀錄的 SOFR 期貨淨空單，但其中部分可能屬基差或避險交易，而非單純看空利率債。美債客戶調查沒那麼偏空，空單小幅減少、中性部位增加，多單不變。若通膨偏弱，這樣的配置可能放大回補；若物價仍強，也可能帶來新一輪賣壓。

4 月貿易數據並未明顯改變展望。商品與服務逆差由修正後的 $566 億縮至 $559 億，略大於市場預估的 $552 億；出口增加 $83 億至 $3,271 億，進口增加 $76 億至 $3,830 億。年度修正改變了追蹤第二季的基準，但相較 Fed 面對的就業與通膨問題，淨改善幅度有限。

國庫券仍呈現眼前現金狀況與較遠政策風險的差異。4、6 與 8 週券債券等值殖利率分別為 3.66%、3.67% 與 3.68%，持平至下跌 2 個基點；52 週券卻上升 8 個基點至 3.90%，月度升幅達 16 個基點。

42 天券標售金額 $650.01 億，最高得標利率 3.600%，投標倍數 3.25，前次較大規模標售為 3.28；間接投標人取得 58.67%，交易商 35.80%。$500 億 364 天券以 3.750% 得標，投標倍數由 3.41 降至 3.34，間接投標人占比升至 68.23%，交易商取得 29.59%。兩者均在 6 月 11 日交割。

附息債需求較強。規模維持 $580 億的 3 年期標售，得標殖利率 4.192%，票息 4.125%，5 月得標殖利率則為 3.965%。投標倍數由 2.54 升至 2.64，間接投標人取得 63.71%，直接投標人 21.01%，交易商僅 15.28%。較高殖利率吸引最終投資人承接，交易商支撐需求有限，交割日在 6 月 15 日。

## 強勢借款人有需求，弱勢企業讓步更多

科技股下跌時，固定收益 ETF 仍上漲。LQD 上漲 0.32%、HYG 上漲 0.10%、JNK 上漲 0.13%、EMB 上漲 0.41%，美債漲勢有利於存續期間較長的持倉。S&P 500 下跌 0.26%，Nasdaq 100 下跌 1.12%，半導體下跌 1.93%，VIX 上升 5.02% 至 19.87。美元下跌 0.14% 至 99.91，黃金下跌 1.75% 至 $4,260。稍早銅價則隨局勢緩和上漲，中國出口在 AI 硬體需求支撐下年增逾 19%。

騰訊發行案較週一的初步計畫更進一步，行銷規模最高 $45 億，包括 10 年與 20 年期美元債，以及 10 年與 30 年期離岸人民幣票據。美元初步指引約為美債加 80 與 90 個基點，人民幣指引約為 2.95% 與 3.55%。上午稍晚，美元訂單超過 $30 億，人民幣需求超過 205 億元；截至報告截止時間，最終規模與定價尚未確定。

騰訊今年有 $35 億、明年有 $28 億債務到期，所得計畫用於再融資與一般用途，包括 AI 發展。公司承諾將年度 AI 投資增加一倍以上，超過人民幣 360 億元。中國保險公司投資離岸人民幣債券的管道擴大，可能增加買家，但美元債仍需在偏高美債殖利率上提供足夠補償。

Bpifrance 專用發行工具行銷首檔 European Secured Note，規模至少 €5 億、天期 5 年，以法國中小企業貸款為擔保。初步指引約為中間交換利率加 42 個基點，訂單超過 €17.5 億。預期 Aaa 評等的雙重追索結構，讓投資人可向發行人與貸款池求償。指引接近 Bpifrance 無擔保 2031 年 6 月券的曲線，最終定價將顯示擔保品、資本計提與監理認可，能否降低中小企業貸款的融資成本。

MSD Investment Corp. 則提供已完成的美國發行案例。這家民間信貸業務發展公司發行 $3 億 3 年期票據，以美債加 240 個基點定價，較初步討論約 270 個基點收窄 30 個基點，預期評等 Baa3 與 BBB−。資金用途為再融資、一般用途及可能的投資組合投資；它是 CPI 公布前發行的八家投資等級借款人之一。

Shutterfly 的 $11.5 億高收益債即使提供 12% 殖利率，仍需增加債權保障。修訂條款限制股利、投資、價值移轉與激進的盈餘加回。訂單超額認購，買方卻不願接受更低殖利率。另有 $5 億定期貸款，以基準加 650 個基點、發行價 96–97 討論，同時搭配 $2.25 億第二順位擔保貸款。

營運表現解釋了買方要求。Shutterfly 3 月底債務 $24 億，第一季營收年減 8% 至 $3.135 億，申報 EBITDA 虧損擴大至 $1,970 萬。即使公司強調實體產品，AI 生成影像與媒體消費習慣改變，仍威脅需求。先前融資已被歸類為困境債務交換，投資人除了高殖利率，也希望更嚴格限制現金流出。

Vedanta 則在資產負債表改善後尋求再融資。計畫中的 $52 億方案，要替換 2028–2033 年到期的 $36 億債券，以及 2028 年起到期的 $16 億貸款。淨債務已由五年前 $89 億降至 $49 億，S&P 與穆迪均上調評等。擬議的 5 年、7 年與 10 年期分期攤還債，可平滑還款日程；管理層希望將約 10% 的借款成本最多降低 300 個基點。

歐洲光纖網路面對的調整更困難。網路擴張未能帶來足夠用戶與現金，困境投資人收購 DNS:Net、G.Network 與 Deutsche Glasfaser 的銀行債權。一家貸款人在 Deutsche Glasfaser 的 €70 億重整中，出售約 €3.5 億貸款；貸方同意將 €17 億債務降為次順位，並提供 €4 億新融資後，股東投入 €8.45 億特別股資金。約 65% 歐洲光纖企業需在兩年內再融資。

CoreWeave 與歐洲高收益債投資人通話，討論可能的美元與歐元發行。其 Ba3/B+/BB− 評等，加上沒有既有歐元高收益債曲線，使比較案例有限。PolarDC 近期 €8 億北歐高收益債，是少數投機等級資料中心發行案；歐洲同類供給仍以投資等級大型雲端業者為主。投資人需衡量稀少供給與租戶集中、槓桿及技術循環風險，單憑 AI 題材還不足以判斷回收前景或融資成本。

## 歐洲產出偏弱，政策壓力仍未消退

德國 4 月工業生產月增 0.4%，前值修正為下跌 0.1%，略低於 0.5% 的預期。營建增加 2.4%，但排除能源與營建的製造業持平，汽車產出下跌 4.7%；整體產出年比及最近三個月比較均下跌 0.5%。核心工業疲弱，延續週一訂單數據的警訊。

法國央行總裁 Emmanuel Moulin 表示，伊朗戰爭的油價衝擊比原先假設更大、更持久，新預測將下修成長、上修通膨。先前法國 2026 年通膨預測為 1.7%，經濟已在第一季萎縮，企業指標也持續惡化。然而，市場仍完全反映 ECB 年內再升息 25 個基點，並傾向之後還有一次。

加拿大 6 月 10 日決策面對不同的先後順序問題。第一季景氣偏弱，市場與經濟學家預期維持利率 2.25%，即使 4 月初估成長 0.4%、5 月就業增加 87,800 人，失業率降至 6.6%。總裁 Tiff Macklem 認為目前利率適合吸收美國關稅衝擊、使通膨回到目標，但警告能源若廣泛轉嫁，可能需要連續升息。最新就業回升，尚未消除經濟學家的衰退疑慮。

日本方面，一名前日銀高層認為企業轉嫁成本加快，政策已落後情勢。10 年期日債殖利率 5 月曾達 2.8%，為 1996 年以來最高，反映市場對財政擴張與延遲緊縮的擔憂。日銀進一步行動會提高日本機構可取得的國內報酬，也改變避險後海外債券的相對吸引力。

財政細節提供部分緩解。日本 ¥3.1 兆追加預算用於通膨與戰爭影響，但不增加曆年發債。政府也提議減少經常性追加預算，聚焦超過 200% 的債務占 GDP 比率。若將計畫納入目前約 ¥122 兆的初始預算，可提高透明度，不過較大的帳面總額仍可能使投資人不安。最終發債路徑，比支出列在哪份預算更重要。

台灣則出現更直接的現金緊縮。5 年期政府債券殖利率跳升 32 個基點至 1.71%，為 2008 年以來最高；10 年期標售殖利率創 2013 年以來最高。季節性繳稅抽走銀行流動性，銀行保留現金，可轉讓定存單餘額降至 2014 年以來最低。通膨高於相關門檻，又在資金壓力上疊加偏緊政策的預期。

Moulin 另指出，擴大歐元國際角色需要更多安全資產，可能包括為國防與 AI 計畫共同舉債。更深的基準債市能吸引準備、交易與發行需求，同時也增加高評等供給，長期與美債競爭資金。

## 升息與債務交易，使新興市場表現分歧

印尼央行非例行升息支撐匯率，卻沒能帶動債券上漲。政策利率提高 25 個基點至 5.5%，三週累計升息 75 個基點。印尼盾回升 0.7%，股市大漲逾 7%，10 年期政府殖利率卻上升 23 個基點至 7.51%。投資人仍質疑財政干預、央行擴大的成長任務與經濟治理。

央行明確希望以較高殖利率吸引外資，但干預已使外匯準備連續第五個月減少。印尼盾在接連創低後，年內仍貶近 8%。Barclays、BNY 與 PT Mega Capital Sekuritas 預期 6 月 18 日會議還會行動，可能再升 50 個基點。較高利息收益暫時打斷匯率跌勢，尚未解決本幣債的信心問題。

肯亞在先前十次、合計 425 個基點降息後，維持利率 8.75%。整體通膨由 5.6% 升至 6.7%，核心由 2.8% 升至 3.2%，柴油與汽油成本自戰爭爆發以來分別上升 40% 與 20%。穩定先令及 $132 億、接近六個月進口的外匯準備提供緩衝，但成長預測仍下修至 4.9%，經常帳赤字預期擴至 GDP 的 3%。

IMF 敦促奈及利亞維持緊縮，當前通膨 15.7%，全年預估平均 16%。它也批評與 First Abu Dhabi Bank 的 $50 億總報酬交換不透明，高擔保品要求與潛在追繳保證金，可能增加財政成本，並限制利率或匯率決策。今年成長 4.1%、2027 年 4.3% 的預測，並未消除這些融資與治理風險。

塞內加爾先前支付票息，仍未恢復市場管道。2031 年美元債殖利率達 24.56%，追平紀錄，硬通貨債相對美債溢價超過 1,500 個基點。S&P 維持 CCC+ 外幣評等的負向展望，融資需求估計接近 GDP 的 30%。未揭露借款使 $18 億 IMF 融資安排遭暫停，計畫尚未恢復，國家仍實質被排除在國際市場之外。

依靠區域融資，則將部分風險移至西非貨幣聯盟銀行，包括國際投資人透過其持有曝險的象牙海岸機構。國內投資人持有約 73% 本幣債務，以存款融資的銀行仍是重要流動性來源。這個基礎有助續借，卻也把主權風險集中在區域金融體系。

尚比亞的債務交易取得進展。政府增加 $6,500 萬爭取反對債權人後，$13.6 億 2053 年美元債收購案支持率超過 75%。報價為每美元面額 84.35 美分，隨參與接近 100%，降向 82.76 美分。全數買回可啟動非洲開發銀行支持的 $6 億債務換發展安排，政府計畫將節省的 $2.75 億投入電網。S&P 將交易視為機會型操作，而非困境交換。

印度正考慮進一步吸引外資，並在 2024 年加入摩根大通新興市場指數後，爭取納入 Bloomberg Aggregate Bond Index。既有指數納入已吸引全球資金進入合格券種；更廣泛的基準管道可分散對國內買家的依賴，但尚未有新的納入決定。

收盤後，智利將四年結構性赤字目標放寬至 GDP 的 1.5%，提高今年赤字預測，並尋求額外 $62 億發債授權。儘管已宣布削減 $20 億支出，這仍會使債務上限增加 36%。政府總債務預估占 GDP 比率，在 2026 年為 43.1%、2028 年 45.4%、2030 年 46.5%，超過官員先前所稱審慎水準 45%。當日油價、美債殖利率與美元下降，普遍有利新興市場債 ETF，但 EMB 一週報酬仍為負；智利的變化則在收盤後新增個別供給與評等疑慮。

## 接下來看 CPI 與長債承接

5 月 CPI 在 6 月 10 日美東時間 08:30 公布，PPI 與初領失業金則在 6 月 11 日同一時間公布。整體 CPI 預估月增 0.5%、年增 4.2%，前值為 0.6% 與 3.8%；核心預估分別為 0.2% 與 2.9%，前值 0.4% 與 2.8%。PPI 最終需求月增率預估 0.7%，排除食品能源為 0.5%，低於修正後前值 1.4% 與 1.0%。

年底前升息已反映在價格，若核心通膨偏弱、初領人數高於前次 22.5 萬人，可能促使空單回補；若物價普遍偏強且就業需求穩定，則支持鷹派選擇權部位。關鍵在能源是否仍主要影響整體物價，或進一步擴散至核心商品、服務與生產者利潤。

財政部將在 6 月 10 日美東 13:00 增額發行 $390 億 10 年期，6 月 11 日 13:00 再發行 $220 億 30 年期。連同已完成 3 年期，三者共 $1,190 億，6 月 15 日交割。通膨公布後的承接，將檢驗週二強勁最終投資人需求能否延伸至更長天期。若數據溫和、投標卻疲弱，供給與交易商承接能力將成為長端更直接的疑慮。

ECB 在 6 月 11 日美東 08:15 決策，市場預期存款利率提高 25 個基點至 2.25%；日銀 6 月 16 日決策則預期將目標提高 25 個基點至約 1.00%。除了當次調整，通膨預測與後續升息指引，也會影響德債、日債及匯市。曲線有序、後續緊縮有限，有助緩解全球存續期間壓力；油價再漲或海外長債需求疲弱，則使反彈更難延續。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Lower Oil Helps Treasuries Rally Ahead of CPI

Treasuries rose on Tuesday as a halt in Iran-Israel strikes sent crude lower and technology shares weakened ahead of US inflation data. The 10-year yield fell 3 basis points to 4.53%, with lower breakeven inflation accounting for most of the move. A $58 billion 3-year auction drew stronger demand than May's sale, helping the market absorb supply at yields elevated by Friday's payroll surprise.

The rally did little to dislodge expectations for a Fed increase. Futures still priced a quarter-point move by year-end, and options buyers sought protection against one or more increases in the coming months. Record hedge-fund shorts in SOFR futures left room for covering if CPI disappointed those hawkish expectations, while cash-market clients had begun moving toward neutral.

Credit demand held up despite the equity decline. Tencent attracted orders for a larger dual-currency offering, MSD Investment Corp. completed a bond sale inside initial guidance, and Shutterfly found buyers only after strengthening protections at a 12% yield. Outside the US, Indonesian bonds fell sharply even after an emergency rate increase supported the rupiah. Lower oil offered common relief, but financing terms, local liquidity and confidence in policy continued to separate borrowers.

## Inflation Compensation Falls, but Hike Bets Remain

WTI dropped 3.40% to $88.20 and Brent fell 2.97% to $91.45 as the pause in strikes eased immediate supply fears. The 10-year breakeven declined 2 basis points to 2.33%, while its real yield fell only 1 to 2.20%. Most of the nominal rally thus came from reduced inflation compensation, leaving real borrowing costs still high: the 10-year real yield was 13 basis points above a week earlier and 27 above a month earlier.

Nominal yields fell by similar amounts across the curve. The 2-year declined 2 basis points to 4.13%, the 5-year dropped 3 to 4.26%, and the 30-year eased 2 to 5.01%. The 2s10s spread narrowed 1 basis point to 40; 2s30s held at 88. The long bond remained above 5%, and the 2-year was still well above the Fed's 3.5%–3.75% policy range.

Over the week, 2-, 5-, 10- and 30-year yields remained higher by 8, 9, 7 and 4 basis points; monthly increases were 23, 24, 15 and 6. The monthly flattening was 8 basis points in 2s10s and 17 in 2s30s. On Tuesday, the 2s5s10s butterfly fell 1 basis point to −14 and 2s10s30s fell 2 to −8. The 5-year real yield held at 1.82%, while 7-, 20- and 30-year real yields declined 1 or 2 basis points.

Overnight-rate options included positions targeting one or possibly two Fed increases by September. Hedge funds had entered the employment release with a record net short in SOFR futures, though some of that exposure may represent basis or hedging trades rather than outright rate views. A Treasury client survey was less bearish, showing a small reduction in shorts, more neutral positions and unchanged longs. That combination leaves the market vulnerable to covering on soft inflation, as well as renewed selling if prices remain strong.

April trade data did not materially change the outlook. The goods-and-services deficit narrowed to $55.9 billion from a revised $56.6 billion, slightly wider than the $55.2 billion consensus. Exports rose $8.3 billion to $327.1 billion and imports increased $7.6 billion to $383.0 billion. Annual revisions changed the starting point for second-quarter tracking, but the net improvement was modest beside the employment and inflation questions facing the Fed.

Bill yields continued to distinguish immediate cash conditions from later policy risk. Four-, six- and eight-week coupon-equivalent yields finished at 3.66%, 3.67% and 3.68%, flat to 2 basis points lower. The 52-week yield instead jumped 8 basis points to 3.90%, bringing its monthly increase to 16 basis points.

The 42-day auction accepted $65.001 billion at a 3.600% high rate, with bid-to-cover of 3.25 against 3.28 on the prior, larger offering. Indirect bidders took 58.67% and dealers 35.80%. The $50 billion 364-day sale cleared at 3.750%, with cover easing to 3.34 from 3.41, indirect participation rising to 68.23% and dealers taking 29.59%. Both settle June 11.

Coupon demand was stronger. The unchanged $58 billion 3-year offering cleared at 4.192% with a 4.125% coupon, compared with a 3.965% auction yield in May. Bid-to-cover improved to 2.64 from 2.54; indirect buyers took 63.71%, direct buyers 21.01% and dealers only 15.28%. End users absorbed the higher-yielding supply with limited dealer support ahead of June 15 settlement.

## Strong Borrowers Find Demand; Weaker Names Concede More

Fixed-income funds gained even as technology shares fell. LQD rose 0.32%, HYG 0.10%, JNK 0.13% and EMB 0.41%, with Treasury gains helping duration-sensitive holdings. The S&P 500 declined 0.26%, Nasdaq 100 lost 1.12% and semiconductors fell 1.93%; VIX increased 5.02% to 19.87. The dollar slipped 0.14% to 99.91 and gold fell 1.75% to $4,260. Earlier, copper rose as tensions eased and Chinese exports grew more than 19% year on year, supported by AI-hardware demand.

Tencent's offering progressed beyond Monday's preliminary plans. It marketed as much as $4.5 billion across 10- and 20-year dollar bonds and 10- and 30-year offshore yuan notes. Initial dollar guidance was about 80 and 90 basis points over Treasuries; yuan guidance was roughly 2.95% and 3.55%. By midmorning, dollar orders exceeded $3 billion and yuan demand topped 20.5 billion yuan. Final size and pricing remained open at the cutoff.

The company has $3.5 billion of debt maturing this year and $2.8 billion next year, and plans to use proceeds for refinancing and general purposes, including AI development. It pledged to more than double annual AI investment to over 36 billion yuan. Expanded access for Chinese insurers to offshore yuan bonds could broaden the buyer base, while dollar investors still require compensation over elevated Treasury yields.

Bpifrance's dedicated vehicle marketed the first European Secured Note, an at-least €500 million 5-year bond backed by French small-company loans. Initial guidance near 42 basis points over mid-swaps attracted orders above €1.75 billion. Expected to be rated Aaa, the dual-recourse structure gives investors claims on both the issuer and the loan pool. Guidance was close to Bpifrance's unsecured June 2031 curve, leaving final pricing to show whether collateral, capital treatment and regulatory recognition could reduce the cost of financing SME loans.

MSD Investment Corp. provided a completed US comparison. The private-credit business development company sold $300 million of 3-year notes at 240 basis points over Treasuries, 30 tighter than initial discussions near 270, with expected Baa3 and BBB− ratings. Proceeds are intended for refinancing, general purposes and possible portfolio investments. It was one of eight investment-grade borrowers issuing ahead of CPI.

Shutterfly needed more protection for lenders even at a 12% yield on its $1.15 billion junk bond. Revised terms restricted dividends, investments, value transfers and aggressive earnings add-backs. The book was oversubscribed, but buyers resisted lower yields. A $500 million term loan was discussed at 650 basis points over its benchmark and an issue price of 96–97, alongside a $225 million second-lien loan.

The operating record helps explain those demands. Shutterfly ended March with $2.4 billion of debt; first-quarter revenue fell 8% to $313.5 million and reported EBITDA losses widened to $19.7 million. AI-generated images and changing media consumption threatened demand, despite the company's emphasis on physical products. Following an earlier financing classified as a distressed exchange, investors wanted tighter control over cash leakage as well as a high yield.

Vedanta approached refinancing from an improved balance sheet. Its planned $5.2 billion package would replace $3.6 billion of bonds due in 2028–2033 and $1.6 billion of loans due from 2028 onward. Net debt had fallen to $4.9 billion from $8.9 billion five years earlier, and both S&P and Moody's had upgraded it. Proposed 5-, 7- and 10-year amortizing bonds could smooth repayments; management sought savings of as much as 300 basis points from borrowing costs near 10%.

European fiber networks faced a harder adjustment. Distressed investors bought bank claims on DNS:Net, G.Network and Deutsche Glasfaser as network expansion failed to generate sufficient subscribers and cash. One lender sold roughly €350 million of Deutsche Glasfaser loans during a €7 billion restructuring. Sponsors supplied €845 million of preferred equity after lenders agreed to subordinate €1.7 billion and provide €400 million of new financing. About 65% of European fiber companies need refinancing within two years.

CoreWeave held calls with European high-yield investors about possible dollar and euro bonds. Its Ba3/B+/BB− ratings and lack of an existing euro high-yield curve make comparisons scarce. PolarDC's recent €800 million Nordic high-yield bond was one of the few speculative-grade data-center deals in a European market dominated by investment-grade hyperscalers. Investors must weigh that scarcity against tenant concentration, leverage and technology-cycle risk; the AI label alone says little about recovery prospects or funding cost.

## Weak European Output Meets Persistent Policy Pressure

Germany's April industrial production rose 0.4% after a revised 0.1% decline, slightly below the 0.5% forecast. Construction increased 2.4%, but manufacturing excluding energy and construction was flat and auto output fell 4.7%. Production was down 0.5% both year on year and over the latest three-month comparison. The weak industrial core added to Monday's poor order figures.

Bank of France Governor Emmanuel Moulin said forthcoming projections would show weaker growth and higher inflation because the Iran war's oil shock was larger and more persistent than assumed. The previous French inflation forecast was 1.7% for 2026; the economy had contracted in the first quarter and business indicators were deteriorating. Markets nonetheless fully priced another quarter-point ECB increase during the year and leaned toward an additional move.

Canada's June 10 decision presents a different sequencing problem. Markets and economists expected a hold at 2.25% after weak first-quarter activity, despite preliminary April growth of 0.4% and May's 87,800 job gain, which brought unemployment to 6.6%. Governor Tiff Macklem described the current rate as appropriate for absorbing US tariffs and returning inflation to target, but warned that generalized energy pass-through could require consecutive increases. The latest labor recovery has not eliminated economists' recession concerns.

In Japan, a former BOJ executive argued that policy was falling behind as companies passed costs to customers more quickly. The 10-year JGB yield had reached 2.8% in May, its highest since 1996, amid concern over fiscal expansion and delayed tightening. Further BOJ action would improve domestic returns available to Japanese institutions and change the relative attraction of hedged overseas bonds.

The fiscal details offered some reassurance. Japan's ¥3.1 trillion supplemental budget addresses inflation and the war without adding to calendar-year bond issuance. The government also proposed reducing routine reliance on extra budgets and focusing on a debt-to-GDP ratio above 200%. Moving spending into an initial budget currently near ¥122 trillion could improve transparency, although a larger headline total might still unsettle investors. The eventual issuance path remains more important than where spending is recorded.

Taiwan experienced a more immediate cash squeeze. Its 5-year government yield jumped 32 basis points to 1.71%, the highest since 2008, while a 10-year auction produced the highest yield since 2013. Seasonal tax payments drained bank liquidity, and outstanding negotiable certificates of deposit fell to their lowest since 2014 as lenders conserved cash. Inflation above the relevant threshold added expectations of restrictive policy to the funding pressure.

Moulin also argued that expanding the euro's international role would require a larger pool of safe assets, potentially including common borrowing for defense and AI projects. A deeper benchmark market could attract reserve, transaction and issuance demand, while adding high-grade supply that competes with Treasuries over time.

## Rate Increases and Debt Deals Split Emerging Markets

Bank Indonesia's off-cycle increase supported the currency but not bonds. The policy rate rose 25 basis points to 5.5%, bringing cumulative increases over three weeks to 75 basis points. The rupiah recovered 0.7% and equities jumped more than 7%, yet the 10-year government yield climbed 23 basis points to 7.51%. Investors continued to question fiscal intervention, the central bank's expanded growth mandate and economic governance.

The bank explicitly sought higher yields to attract foreign inflows as intervention reduced reserves for a fifth consecutive month. The rupiah was still nearly 8% weaker for the year after successive record lows. Barclays, BNY and PT Mega Capital Sekuritas expected another move at the June 18 meeting, potentially a further 50 basis points. Higher carry had interrupted the currency's decline without resolving the confidence problem in local bonds.

Kenya held at 8.75% after ten reductions totaling 425 basis points. Headline inflation rose to 6.7% from 5.6% and core inflation to 3.2% from 2.8%, with diesel and gasoline costs up 40% and 20% since the war began. A stable shilling and $13.2 billion of reserves, covering almost six months of imports, provided a buffer. Growth was nevertheless revised down to 4.9% and the current-account deficit was expected to widen to 3% of GDP.

The IMF urged Nigeria to keep policy tight with inflation at 15.7% and expected to average 16% during the year. It also criticized the opacity of a $5 billion total-return swap with First Abu Dhabi Bank. High collateral requirements and potential margin calls could create fiscal costs and constrain rate or exchange-rate decisions. Growth forecasts of 4.1% this year and 4.3% in 2027 did not remove those financing and governance risks.

Senegal's earlier coupon payments had not restored market access. Its 2031 dollar yield reached a record-matching 24.56% and the hard-currency premium exceeded 1,500 basis points over Treasuries. S&P retained a negative outlook on the CCC+ foreign-currency rating, with financing needs estimated near 30% of GDP. The unresolved IMF program after undisclosed borrowing and the suspension of a $1.8 billion facility left the sovereign effectively excluded from international markets.

Reliance on regional funding transfers some exposure into banks across the West African monetary union, including Ivorian institutions through which international investors hold claims. Domestic investors own about 73% of local debt, and deposit-funded banks remain an important source of liquidity. That base helps rollover but concentrates sovereign risk within the regional financial system.

Zambia made progress on a long-running debt transaction. Support for the tender of its $1.36 billion 2053 dollar bond exceeded 75% after the government added $65 million to bring holdouts on board. The offer was 84.35 cents on the dollar, declining toward 82.76 as participation approached 100%. A full buyback would unlock a $600 million African Development Bank-backed debt-for-development swap; Zambia planned to direct $275 million of savings to the electricity grid. S&P called the transaction opportunistic rather than distressed.

India was considering further steps to attract foreign investors and gain entry to the Bloomberg Aggregate Bond Index after joining JPMorgan's emerging-market benchmark in 2024. Existing inclusion had already brought global funds into eligible securities. Broader access could diversify demand beyond domestic buyers, though no new inclusion decision had been completed.

After the close, Chile relaxed its four-year structural-deficit goal to 1.5% of GDP, increased the current-year deficit forecast and sought authority for another $6.2 billion of bond sales. That would raise the debt ceiling by 36% despite $2 billion of announced spending cuts. Gross debt was projected at 43.1% of GDP in 2026, 45.4% in 2028 and 46.5% in 2030, above the 45% level officials had described as prudent. The change adds a country-specific supply and rating concern after a session in which lower oil, lower Treasury yields and a weaker dollar had broadly helped EM funds, though EMB's weekly return remained negative.

## CPI and Long-Bond Demand Are Next

May CPI arrives at 08:30 ET on June 10, followed by PPI and jobless claims at the same time on June 11. Headline CPI is forecast to rise 0.5% monthly and 4.2% yearly, after 0.6% and 3.8%; core is expected at 0.2% and 2.9%, after 0.4% and 2.8%. PPI forecasts are 0.7% for final demand and 0.5% excluding food and energy, below revised monthly gains of 1.4% and 1.0%.

With a year-end hike already priced, softer core inflation and claims above the prior 225,000 could encourage shorts to cover. Broad price pressure alongside stable labor demand would instead support the hawkish options positions. The important distinction is whether energy remains a headline effect or spreads further through core goods, services and producer margins.

Treasury reopens $39 billion of 10-year notes at 13:00 ET on June 10 and $22 billion of 30-year bonds at 13:00 on June 11. Including the completed 3-year sale, the three issues settle June 15 for $119 billion gross. Their reception will show whether Tuesday's strong end-user demand extends to longer duration after the inflation releases. Weak bidding despite benign data would make supply and dealer capacity a more immediate concern for the long end.

The ECB decision is due June 11 at 08:15 ET, with consensus expecting a 25-basis-point deposit-rate increase to 2.25%. The BOJ decision on June 16 is expected to raise its target 25 basis points to about 1.00%. Beyond those moves, inflation projections and guidance on further increases will matter for Bunds, JGBs and currency markets. Orderly curves and contained follow-up guidance would ease the pressure on global duration; renewed oil gains or poor overseas long-bond demand would make that relief harder to sustain.
